lead: A map screen does not draw roads or labels. The app tells a map SDK where to look; the SDK fetches square tiles over HTTPS and paints them. The app adds its own shops, riders or customers as markers. Building tiles, projection and zoom yourself takes months, so apps reuse the SDK. Ride-hailing, food delivery and station finders work this way.
prereq: You need Unit 2 fragments, Unit 3 basic views, and the manifest idea from Unit 2.

sections.h3: Fragment, view and the API key

items: MapFragment or SupportMapFragment owns the map lifecycle; reach the map in onMapReady.
MapView is a plain View; forward onResume, onPause and onDestroy to it or the map leaks.
API key: created in the cloud console, restricted to package name and signing SHA-1, pasted into AndroidManifest.xml as a meta-data entry named com.google.android.geo.API_KEY.

blocks.text: A missing or wrong key raises no error. The map shows a grey grid. setMapType picks MAP_TYPE_NORMAL, SATELLITE, HYBRID or TERRAIN.
LatLng(latitude, longitude) holds a point in degrees: latitude runs −90 to +90, longitude −180 to +180.

blocks.where: lat_max and lat_min are the largest and smallest marker latitudes in degrees; longitude uses the same formulas. Build a LatLngBounds with new LatLngBounds.Builder().include(new LatLng(lat_min, lon_min)).include(new LatLng(lat_max, lon_max)).build(); south-west corner is (lat_min, lon_min), north-east corner is (lat_max, lon_max).

items: newLatLngZoom(point, zoom) recentres and zooms: 0 is the whole world, 21 a single building.
newLatLngBounds(bounds, padding) fits every marker with a screen margin in pixels.

blocks.text: moveCamera jumps instantly; animateCamera glides. A marker is MarkerOptions().position(p).title("Shop").snippet("Open till 9"); tapping it opens the info window.

sections.h3: Wiring the map into an activity

items: Add the play-services-maps dependency and the INTERNET permission.
Create the API key and restrict it to the package and SHA-1.
Declare a <meta-data> element with android:name="com.google.android.geo.API_KEY" and android:value="YOUR_KEY" inside the <application> element of AndroidManifest.xml.
Put a SupportMapFragment in the layout XML with an id.
The activity implements OnMapReadyCallback; in onCreate get the fragment by id with getSupportFragmentManager().findFragmentById(R.id.map) and call getMapAsync(this) on it.
In onMapReady set the map type, add markers, then move the camera.
For MapView, forward onResume, onPause, onDestroy and onLowMemory.

blocks.text: Markers are not kept by the saved view state. After a rotation add them again, or the screen returns empty.

examples.question: A map screen must show three markers at (12.0, 77.0), (12.1, 77.2) and (11.9, 77.1). Find the camera centre and the latitude and longitude spans so all three fit.
examples.answer: Move the camera to LatLng(12.0, 77.1) and choose a zoom that covers a 0.2° span in both directions, i.e. about 22 km north to south.
examples.check:
lats = [12.0, 12.1, 11.9]
lons = [77.0, 77.2, 77.1]
print(round((max(lats) + min(lats)) / 2, 1))
print(round((max(lons) + min(lons)) / 2, 1))
print(round(max(lats) - min(lats), 1))
print(round(max(lons) - min(lons), 1))

traps: Swapping the arguments. LatLng takes latitude first; new LatLng(77.0, 12.0) moves a shop near Bengaluru (12.0° N, 77.0° E) into the Arctic, and the map still draws, so the bug survives testing.
Calling getMap() in onCreate gives null. Use getMapAsync and add markers in onMapReady.
A wrong or missing API key shows a grey grid, not an error. Check the meta-data name and that Maps SDK for Android is enabled.
A MapView that never forwards onPause, onResume and onDestroy leaks the map and can crash on return.

Zoom is a scale factor: each step doubles the scale, it is not a span in degrees, and it may be fractional. Use CameraUpdateFactory.newLatLngBounds to fit a degree span instead of guessing a zoom number.

quiz.q: Name the two ways to place a Google map on an Android screen.
Why must markers be added inside onMapReady rather than onCreate?
quiz.a: getMapAsync is asynchronous; the GoogleMap object does not exist until the callback fires, so an earlier call returns null.

quiz.q: A marker is created as new LatLng(80.2, 13.1). What is wrong, and what is the correct call?
quiz.a: The arguments are swapped: 80.2 is being read as a latitude, so the marker lands near the pole instead of near Chennai. Both numbers are individually legal, which is why no error is raised. Write new LatLng(13.1, 80.2).

quiz.q: Markers sit at (13.0, 80.0) and (13.2, 80.4). Give the camera centre and both spans.
quiz.a: Latitude centre (13.2 + 13.0) ÷ 2 = 13.1°; longitude centre (80.4 + 80.0) ÷ 2 = 80.2°; latitude span 0.2°; longitude span 0.4°.

quiz.q: The code is correct but the map is a grey grid. Give three causes and how each is checked.
quiz.a: The API key meta-data is missing or misnamed; the key is not enabled for Maps SDK for Android; the key is restricted to a different package name or SHA-1 certificate. Check the manifest entry, the console's API list and the restriction entries.

quiz.q: Rotate the phone and the markers disappear. Explain why and give the fix.
quiz.a: Rotation destroys and recreates the activity; markers were added in code and are not part of the saved view hierarchy. Either re-add them in onMapReady after recreation or keep the map in a retained fragment.

beyond: Not for the exam. Production apps use vector tiles, custom styling, marker clustering and offline caches. MapLibre with OpenStreetMap data and Mapbox are common alternatives. Compose wraps the same SDK declaratively. Search: marker clustering, newLatLngBounds with padding, offline maps.
